title: Re-work commit-message editing to route edits into the implementable review
description:
The UI commit-message editor works and captures edits in the right shape, but the edits are POSTed to /api/record-feedback (the pattern-analysis snapshot in ~/.umpire/feedback/) instead of /api/review (the per-review deliverable in .umpire/reviews/ that an agent implements). Result, editing a commit message never affects the commit, because nothing acts on an individual snapshot.

Rework decisions (confirmed with user). Route commit-message edits into the review output ONLY (.umpire/reviews/review-*.json) and stop writing them to the analysis snapshot. Represent them as a dedicated structured field (commit_message_edits array) on the review. Keep editing BOTH subject (title) and body, so the implementing agent rewrites the full message.

An agent reading the review JSON then rewrites the commit message as part of implementing the feedback. The existing frontend collectCommitMessageEdits() already emits sha plus original_subject, original_body, edited_subject, edited_body, with original included for agent context.
close_reason: Epic complete. Commit-message edits now route into the implementable review deliverable (.umpire/reviews/) as a dedicated commit_message_edits field carrying both subject and body, and no longer into the pattern-analysis snapshot. Delivered across umpire-2le (model and handler), umpire-g7k (frontend submit plus relaxed guard), umpire-wq6 (snapshot removal), and umpire-14p (review checkpoint). Commits 0bf33f9, d359720, a018e5b, 3939536.

title: Add a CI workflow running build/test/vet on push and pull_request
description:
Today .github/workflows/ has only release.yml (triggered on v* tags). Nothing runs on push or pull_request. Deferred because no outside contributors are expected yet, so per-PR checks would only gate commits by Zach. Accepted consequence -- nothing automatically prevents a regression of the SEC-1 loopback bind or the SEC-2 host/origin middleware. Their regression tests exist but must be run locally (go test ./...) rather than enforced by a check.

When implemented: a workflow on push/pull_request running go build ./..., go test ./..., go vet ./..., and gofmt -l. Four notes. (1) gofmt -l lists offending files but exits 0, so a naive step never fails -- assert on empty output (or use -exec false), or the lint step is decoration. (2) Pin setup-go with go-version-file: go.mod so CI tracks the toolchain floor rather than drifting from it. (3) Skip golangci-lint initially -- its default linters will flag existing code, meaning a cleanup pass or a suppression config. Add it deliberately when someone will fix what it finds. (4) CI only works if the check is required by branch protection -- advisory-only CI gets ignored once it goes red, which is a GitHub settings change, not code.

Reference: audit doc Part 2, Bead B (PROD-1). Revisit when people other than Zach start opening PRs.

title: Add internal/feedback package — data model and storage
description:
Create internal/feedback/ package with three files:

**snapshot.go**: Snapshot struct and SubmitRequest struct.
- Snapshot fields: Version (int), CreatedAt (time.Time), RepoPath (string), BaseRef, HeadRef, BaseSHA, HeadSHA (strings), Diff (string), Review (embedded struct with Summary string + Comments []review.Comment).
- SubmitRequest fields: Diff (string), Review (same embedded struct) — this is the JSON body the frontend POSTs.

**store.go**: Store struct with Dir field (string, defaults to ~/.umpire/feedback/).
- Save(s *Snapshot) (string, error): MkdirAll the Dir, set CreatedAt/Version, marshal to JSON, write to snapshot-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json. Return path.
- Count() (int, error): Glob for snapshot-*.json files in Dir, return count.

**prompt.go**: GeneratePrompt(count int) string: Build a self-contained prompt string for the user to paste into Claude Code. The prompt instructs Claude to:
1. Read all JSON files in ~/.umpire/feedback/
2. For each snapshot, understand the diff and review comments
3. Classify feedback as generalizable preferences vs one-off corrections — only patterns produce config changes
4. Look for recurring themes: naming conventions, error handling style, architectural preferences, testing expectations
5. Read existing user-level config: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/settings.json
6. Propose additions/edits without duplicating or contradicting existing rules — user-level config only
7. Present proposed changes for approval before applying
8. After changes applied, delete processed snapshot files from ~/.umpire/feedback/
The prompt should embed the count so Claude knows how many snapshots to expect.

**Tests**: store_test.go covering Save (writes valid JSON, sets version/timestamp) and Count (returns correct count including zero case).

title: Add post-submission feedback flow in frontend
description:
Modify the frontend to handle the post-submission feedback recording flow.

**Changes to web/static/js/app.js — submitReview():**

After the review is saved, instead of showing 'Server shutting down...' immediately, render a multi-step inline flow in the submit bar:

Step 1: Show success + question:
  'Review saved to <path>'
  'Record this feedback to improve future Claude sessions?  [Yes] [No thanks]'

Step 2a — No thanks: POST /api/shutdown, show 'Server shutting down...'

Step 2b — Yes (threshold not reached): POST /api/record-feedback with {diff: App.fullDiff, review: {summary, comments}}. Show 'Feedback recorded (N of 5 until analysis is available). Server shutting down...' Then POST /api/shutdown.

Step 2c — Yes (threshold reached): Same POST, then show 'Feedback recorded — N snapshots available. Generate a prompt to analyze your feedback and propose Claude config updates? [Copy Prompt to Clipboard] [Not now]'
  - Copy Prompt: GET /api/feedback-prompt, copy prompt text to clipboard via navigator.clipboard.writeText(), then POST /api/shutdown
  - Not now: POST /api/shutdown

**Cache the full diff:**
In loadFullDiff(), after fetching the diff, store it as this.fullDiff = diff. This makes the base..head diff available at submission time for the feedback snapshot.

**New API methods in web/static/js/api.js:**
- recordFeedback({diff, review}): POST /api/record-feedback, return JSON
- getFeedbackPrompt(): GET /api/feedback-prompt, return JSON
- shutdown(): POST /api/shutdown

**CSS in web/static/css/app.css:**
Style the feedback question and buttons to match the existing submit bar aesthetic. The buttons should use existing .btn, .btn-submit, and .btn-cancel classes. Add a .feedback-message class for the status text with color: var(--text-secondary) and margin-top: 0.25rem.

title: Embed a body line-wrapping instruction in the saved review JSON for edited commit messages
description:
Problem: When a reviewer rewrites a commit message during review, the edits are captured as commit_message_edits and saved to the review JSON (internal/review/review.go CommitMessageEdit, assembled in internal/server/handlers.go handleReview near line 96, written by internal/review/store.go to .umpire/reviews/review-TIMESTAMP.json). Nothing in the saved file tells the applying agent to re-wrap the body, so an agent applying an edit could write a long, unwrapped body.

Goal: Embed an agent-facing instruction in the review JSON, populated only when commit message edits are present, telling the agent to apply standard git commit-message line-wrapping (hard-wrap the body at 72 columns) to any commit message it edits.

Scope note (from Zach): instruct ONLY the body line-wrapping and line-length rule. Do NOT mention subject length.

Recommended approach: add a field to the Review struct, for example CommitMessageEditInstructions string with json tag commit_message_edit_instructions,omitempty, and set it in handleReview only when len(req.CommitMessageEdits) is greater than 0. Wording is at the implementer's discretion -- keep it concise, along the lines of: When applying these commit message edits, hard-wrap the body at 72 columns, per standard git commit conventions. Because CommitMessageEdits already uses omitempty, the review JSON stays clean for reviews that make no message edits.

Also tighten the CommitMessageEdit doc comment (internal/review/review.go near lines 18-27) to reference the same 72-column rule, so the documented contract and the emitted file agree. Optional but recommended.

Files: internal/review/review.go (Review struct plus the CommitMessageEdit doc comment), internal/server/handlers.go (handleReview near line 96). Tests: internal/server/handlers_test.go and/or internal/review/store_test.go -- add a case asserting the instruction is present when edits exist and omitted when they do not.

Verify: submit a review with a commit-message edit and confirm the saved review-TIMESTAMP.json includes the instruction field. Submit one without edits and confirm the field is omitted.

title: Restore the "Files changed" sidebar tab with working file navigation and rename support
description:
The "Files changed" sidebar tab was hidden (its button removed from sidebar.js init) to eliminate a broken interaction (BUG-1). renderFiles, scrollToFile, API.getFiles, and the /api/files endpoint remain in place but unreachable, so restoring the tab is close to a one-line revert. This bead covers restoring it correctly AND fixing the rename parsing bug (BUG-2) that the tab depends on. File one bead for both because they are coupled -- the BUG-2 parser fix depends on a rendering contract that only exists once the tab is back.

BUG-1 (file-switcher does nothing in per-commit view): The tab is populated from GET /api/files (every file changed across base..head), but the rendered diff on load (and when a single commit is selected) contains only one commit files. Clicking a file from a different commit finds no matching DOM node, so scrollToFile silently does nothing. Agreed fix (decided 2026-08-12) -- clicking a file should ALWAYS put the user in the full-range view. On click: (1) if not already showing the full diff, call App.loadFullDiff() and clear Sidebar.activeCommitSHA. (2) WAIT for the re-render to complete, THEN scrollToFile(path). loadFullDiff fetches /api/diff and re-renders via diff2html, so calling scrollToFile synchronously after it searches a stale DOM and reproduces the no-op. Chain off the render, do NOT fire-and-forget (most likely step to get wrong). (3) if already in full-diff view, skip the reload and just scroll. Also make scrollToFile console.warn on a miss instead of being a silent no-op. Add regression coverage for clicking a file that lives in a non-active commit.

BUG-2 (renamed files mishandled by --name-status parsing) in internal/git/git.go ChangedFiles(): git diff --name-status emits THREE tab-separated fields for a rename or copy -- Rxxx TAB old TAB new. SplitN(line, TAB, 2) collapses this into Status=Rxxx and Path=(old TAB new). Impact once the tab is back: statusLabels lookup misses (shows raw R100), and Path contains an embedded tab plus both paths so it never matches diff2html .d2h-file-name. Fix: split into up to three fields, strip the similarity score from R/C statuses, use the NEW path as Path (optionally keep old path for display), add a unit test with a rename fixture. Confirm the chosen Path matches what diff2html renders as the file name (it renders a rename header roughly as old-arrow-new), which is why this waits for the tab. Latent today -- /api/files is unreachable, and the only other caller (cmd/root.go changed-files count) reads only len(files), which stays correct.

Reference: audit doc Part 2, Bead A.

title: Auto-size the commit-message pane to a standard git commit-message width
description:
Problem: When traversing commits, the commit-message pane (#commit-header, web/static/css/app.css:200) has a fixed default width of 25vw. A commit body is hard-wrapped at ~72 columns with real newlines and is rendered in .commit-message-body -- a pre element with white-space pre-wrap and font-family inherit (a proportional font) at app.css:339. Because the pane is usually narrower than a 72-column line, each hard-wrapped source line ALSO soft-wraps inside the pane, producing a ragged double-wrapped look.

Goal: Default the pane width so a standard-formatted commit body (72-column hard wrap) fits without soft-wrapping, and keep that width consistent as the user navigates between commits. Preserve the existing drag-to-resize (Resize.attachCommitHeaderDrag in web/static/js/resize.js) as the user override, so the user can adjust the width from there.

Recommended approach (CSS-first): render .commit-message-body in a monospace font and cap its wrap width at 72 columns (width 72ch), then let #commit-header hug that width (width fit-content or max-content) with a viewport-capped max-width and the existing min-width. A monospace 72ch is an exact, font-relative measure, so the pane chrome (pane padding 0.75rem 1rem, plus the .commit-message padding and border) falls out naturally. Switch the edit textarea .commit-message-body-input (app.css:309) to monospace too, so editing matches the rendered width.

Alternative if fit-content fights the sticky or flex layout: measure a 72-char monospace string in JS inside renderCommitHeader (web/static/js/app.js:152) and set header.style.width, clamped to the Resize MIN/MAX bounds. That matches the existing JS-driven sizing style.

Note: the pane is torn down and rebuilt on every commit navigation (removeCommitHeader then renderCommitHeader), so a manual drag width already resets when moving between commits. This change does not regress that. If width persistence across navigation is wanted, file a separate follow-up.

Files: web/static/css/app.css (#commit-header near line 200, .commit-message-body near 339, .commit-message-body-input near 309). Possibly web/static/js/app.js:152 (renderCommitHeader) and web/static/js/resize.js (MIN or MAX bounds).

Verify: run umpire in a repo with multi-line commit bodies. Confirm each 72-column source line renders as a single visual line, the pane width is consistent across commits, and dragging still resizes.
